blocks.title: Understand
blocks.text: Client-side JavaScript can offer immediate feedback and responsive interfaces, but its validation can be bypassed or altered.

blocks.title: Apply
blocks.text: Server-side code enforces permissions, validates input against business rules and updates authoritative records or databases.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Processing choices trade off device load, server load, confidentiality, latency, accessibility and reliability; many systems use both.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict first
blocks.text: An attacker can skip the browser form and send a request containing quantity=1000.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain
blocks.text: The server must enforce actual constraints; browser checks are useful but only improve convenience.

blocks.title: Predict first
blocks.text: The browser can preview or resize an image to reduce traffic and improve usability.

blocks.title: Explain
blocks.text: The server verifies authorisation, validates the uploaded bytes and applies safe storage rules.
